identity_notes: Broccoli evidence in this scope (53 kept of 117 screened) splits into three groups that should not be conflated: (1) whole-broccoli/broccoli-sprout trials, (2) isolated-sulforaphane or isolated-glucoraphanin trials (flagged related_form_differs -- the bioactive precursor/metabolite is not the same as eating the intact vegetable, and bioavailability differs substantially by cooking method: raw broccoli gave 37% sulforaphane bioavailability vs lower for cooked in 18950181), and (3) broad cruciferous-vegetable-family observational/epidemiological reviews (23211939, 24341734, 38051036, 38892516, 32086800, 33919894, 39741515) that are NOT broccoli-specific and are largely dietary-intake-association data, not supplementation RCTs -- flagged related_form_differs throughout. A large share of retrieved primary-trial abstracts were truncated in this scope before the results sentence, leaving many otherwise on-topic RCTs (e.g., 15387326 H. pylori, 21559038 T2D oxidative stress, 27130714 asthma, 35475592 breast cancer presurgical) with direction_primary 'unresolved' -- full abstracts should be re-pulled before drawing conclusions. Two clear null/negative primary findings stand out: broccoli sprouts did NOT improve endothelial function in human hypertension despite a positive rat-model precedent (20805984), and sulforaphane/broccoli-sprout homogenate did NOT protect against neutrophilic airway inflammation or induce antioxidant genes in a proof-of-concept study (27450419). A 12-week RCT specifically addressed the long-suspected thyroidal-toxicity concern with sulforaphane and reported a null/safe result by title (30735751) -- key safety handoff. Several trials combine broccoli/sulforaphane with exercise training in a factorial design (34579020, 40944125, 42228225) or with another active agent (methylphenidate in 41604557, standard antibiotic therapy in 31830776), so broccoli's isolated contribution cannot be determined from the retrieved abstract alone.
